facts.statement: Peasants discovered a Telmatosaurus skull in 1895 at the Săcele estate in Transylvania and gave it to Ilona Nopcsa.
facts.quote: In 1895 some peasants presented Ilona Nopcsa, the daughter of their lord, with a dinosaur skull they had found at the estate Săcele in the district Hunedoara (then named Hunyad) in Transylvania.

facts.statement: Franz Nopcsa originally named the species Limnosaurus transsylvanicus in 1899.
facts.quote: In 1899 Nopcsa named the skull Limnosaurus transsylvanicus.

facts.statement: Nopcsa renamed the genus Telmatosaurus in 1903 after finding that Limnosaurus was already used for a crocodilian described in 1872.
facts.quote: Later Nopcsa discovered that the name Limnosaurus had already been used by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1872 for a crocodilian (later reclassified as Pristichampsus), so in 1903 Nopcsa renamed the genus Telmatosaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil, consisting of a skull and lower jaws, dates to about 68 million years ago from the Maastrichtian age of the Haţeg Island.
facts.quote: The holotype, NHMUK PV R 3386 (previously referred to as BMNH R 3386), was found in the Haţeg Basin in a layer of the Sânpetru Formation dating from the Maastrichtian, about 68 million years old, at the time part of the Haţeg Island, one of the islands of the European Archipelago.

facts.statement: Nopcsa transferred the species to the genus Orthomerus in 1915, naming it Orthomerus transsylvanicus.
facts.quote: In 1915 Nopcsa referred his species to the genus Orthomerus, as an Orthomerus transsylvanicus.

facts.statement: The name Telmatosaurus was revived in the 1980s because the genus Orthomerus was considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: However, since the 1980s, Orthomerus has been considered a nomen dubium, leading to a revival of the name Telmatosaurus.

facts.statement: Telmatosaurus measured about 5 meters in length and 600 kg in mass, a size attributed to insular dwarfism.
facts.quote: It was relatively small for its group, measuring approximately 5 m in length and 600 kg in body mass, which has been explained as an instance of insular dwarfism.

facts.statement: Telmatosaurus transsylvanicus lived between 70 and 66 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Telmatosaurus transsylvanicus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Telmatosaurus (del griego "lagarto de pantano"), un dinosaurio ornitópodo hadrosáurido basal que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, entre 70 a 66 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: The skull of Telmatosaurus was about 40 centimeters long, narrow, and quite high at the back.
facts.quote: El cráneo, de unos 40 centímetros de largo, es estrecho y bastante alto en la parte posterior.

facts.statement: The teeth of Telmatosaurus were high and narrow, about four millimeters wide.
facts.quote: Los dientes son altos y estrechos, de unos cuatro milímetros de ancho.

facts.statement: Telmatosaurus ate C3 plants, shrubs, herbaceous plants, leaves, and seeds.
facts.quote: Telmatosaurus comía plantas C3, arbustos, plantas herbáceas, hojas y semillas.

facts.statement: The presence of an ameloblastoma in a dinosaur suggests that benign tumor development is a basal characteristic.
facts.quote: The discovery of an ameloblastoma in a dinosaur gives evidence that the development of benign tumors is a basal characteristic, not just a relatively modern condition.

facts.statement: Because only the lower jaws are preserved, the cause of death for the juvenile Telmatosaurus with the tumor cannot be determined.
facts.quote: Since its preserved remains consist of only the two lower jaws, no one can ascertain its cause of death.

facts.statement: Magyar and colleagues named the clade containing Telmatosaurus, Kryptohadros, and Tethyshadros as Telmatosauridae.
facts.quote: Magyar et al. named the group containing these three genera as the new clade Telmatosauridae.

facts.statement: The family classification of Telmatosaurus is listed as Hadrosauridae with uncertainty.
facts.quote: familia: Hadrosauridae?

facts.statement: It is debated whether fragmentary hadrosauroid material from Spain, France, Germany, and Romania belongs to Telmatosaurus, as an identity is difficult to prove.
facts.quote: Fragmentary hadrosauroid material from Spain, France and Germany, that had been referred to Orthomerus, is now often assigned to Telmatosaurus, but an identity is hard to prove; the same is also true of many Romanian fragments and eggs.

facts.statement: The first remains of this dinosaur were found in Romania.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de este dinosaurio fueron encontrados en Rumanía.

facts.statement: In 1899, Nopcsa named the skull Limnosaurus transsylvanicus.
facts.quote: En 1899 Nopcsa nombró al cráneo como Limnosaurus transsylvanicus.

facts.statement: Nopcsa renamed the genus Telmatosaurus in 1903 after discovering that Limnosaurus had previously been used for a crocodile by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1872.
facts.quote: Posteriormente Nopcsa descubrió que el nombre Limnosaurus también había sido usado por Othniel Charles Marsh en 1872 para designar a un cocodrilo, que más tarde fue reclasificado como Pristichampsus, así que en 1903 cambió el nombre por Telmatosaurus.

facts.statement: The generic name derives from the Greek word for 'swamp', reflecting the belief that the animal had aquatic habits.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico deriva del griego λιμνή, limnè, "pantano", al creer que el animal tenía hábitos acuáticos.

facts.statement: In 1910, Barnum Brown named the genus Hecatasaurus, unaware of the name change, creating a later synonym.
facts.quote: En 1910 Barnum Brown, desconociendo el reemplazo del nombre, bautizó al género como Hecatasaurus, siendo este un sinónimo más moderno.

facts.statement: In 1915, Nopcsa included this species in the genus Orthomerus as Orthomerus transsylvanicus.
facts.quote: En 1915 Nopcsa incluyó esta especie en el género Orthomerus, como Orthomerus transsylvanicus.

facts.statement: In the 1980s, paleontologists revived Telmatosaurus transylvanicus after considering it dubious, and in 1984 Orthomerus dolloi was renamed Telmatosaurus dolloi, though this name is invalid due to priority of Orthomerus.
facts.quote: En la década de 1980, sin embargo, los paleontologos empezaron a ver que esta forma era un dudosa. Esto llevó a Telmatosaurus transylvanicus a ser revivido y en 1984 Orthomerus dolloi incluso fue rebautizado como Telmatosaurus dolloi, aunque ese no puede ser un nombre válido porque Orthomerus tiene prioridad.

facts.statement: In 1900, Nopcsa assigned Telmatosaurus to Trachodontidae, a term that is no longer used.
facts.quote: En 1900, Nopcsa asignó Telmatosaurus a Trachodontidae, un término que ya no se usa.

facts.statement: Current cladistic analyses suggest Telmatosaurus is either a basal member of Hadrosauridae or occupies a basal position in the broader Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: En los análisis cladísticos actuales, Telmatosaurus parece ser un miembro basal de Hadrosauridae u ocupa una posición basal en el más amplio Hadrosauroidea.

facts.statement: The parent group of Telmatosaurus is Telmatosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Telmatosauridae

facts.statement: The family of Telmatosaurus is Telmatosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Telmatosauridae

facts.statement: Telmatosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The holotype dates to about 68 million years ago, from the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Tiene una antigüedad de unos 68 millones de años, datando del Maastrichtiense.

facts.statement: At that time, the land where the fossils were found was part of the European archipelago.
facts.quote: En aquella época estos terrenos formaban parte del archipiélago europeo.

facts.statement: The time range for Telmatosaurus is from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype, BMNH B.3386, a skull with a lower jaw, was found in the Haţeg Basin in a layer of the Sânpetru Formation.
facts.quote: El holotipo, BMNH B.3386, un cráneo con mandíbula inferior, fue encontrado en la cuenca Haţeg en una capa de la Formación Sânpetru.

facts.statement: Romanian findings include a set of four cervical vertebrae (BMNH R3841), three sacral vertebrae with two sacral ribs (BMNH R4911), and some loose vertebrae and upper jaws.
facts.quote: Los hallazgos de Rumania también incluyen un conjunto de cuatro vértebras cervicales, espécimen BMNH R3841, tres vértebras sacras con dos costillas sacras, BMNH R4911 y algunas vértebras sueltas y mandíbulas superiores.

facts.statement: A juvenile Telmatosaurus examined by Dumbrava et al. has a large non-cancerous tumor called ameloblastoma in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Un Telmatosaurus juvenil examinado por Dumbrava et al. tiene un gran tumor no canceroso llamado ameloblastoma en la mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: The presence of this benign tumor in a dinosaur is a novelty, as ameloblastomas were previously only known in modern mammals and reptiles.
facts.quote: La presencia de este tumor benigno en un dinosaurio es una novedad, ya que antes del descubrimiento, los ameloblastomas solo se conocían en los mamíferos modernos y los reptiles.

facts.statement: Since the preserved remains consist only of the two lower jaws, no one can determine the cause of its death.
facts.quote: Dado que sus restos conservados consisten solo en las dos mandíbulas inferiores, nadie puede determinar la causa de su muerte.

facts.statement: It is debated whether fragmentary material from Spain, France, and Germany, previously included in Orthomerus, truly belongs to Telmatosaurus, as it is difficult to prove the identity.
facts.quote: Posteriormente material fragmentario perteneciente a hadrosauridos de España, Francia y Alemania, que se incluía en Orthomerus, es ahora asignado como Telmatosaurus, pero es difícil probar que realmente este material pertenezca a este género, al igual que ocurre con algunos fragmentos de huevo encontrados en Rumanía.

facts.statement: Some material was lost during World War II due to bombings, complicating the study of the species.
facts.quote: Parte del material se perdió durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial por los bombardeos.
